# --- scripthub ---
# name: Hello (Python)
# description: "The smallest useful script: a few parameters passed as --flags. Start here."
# category: Basics
# parameters:
#   - name: name
#     label: Name
#     type: text
#     default: World
#     required: true
#     max_length: 60
#   - name: greeting
#     label: Greeting
#     type: select
#     choices: [Hello, Hi, Good morning, Namaste]
#     default: Hello
#   - name: times
#     label: Times
#     type: number
#     default: 1
#     min: 1
#     max: 10
#   - name: shout
#     label: Shout
#     type: boolean
#     default: false
#     help: Upper case
# --- end scripthub ---
"""Greet someone. ScriptHub calls it as: hello.py --name World --greeting Hello --times 1 [--shout]"""
import argparse

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
parser.add_argument("--name", default="World")
parser.add_argument("--greeting", default="Hello")
parser.add_argument("--times", type=int, default=1)
parser.add_argument("--shout", action="store_true")
args = parser.parse_args()

line = f"{args.greeting}, {args.name}!"
if args.shout:
    line = line.upper()
for _ in range(args.times):
    print(line)

source.text:
# --- scripthub ---
# name: Succeed, fail or take a while
# description: Prints a line per second, then ends the way you choose. Use it to try the live console, Stop, Trace and Debug, and the success / failure arrows of a sequence.
# category: Basics
# parameters:
#   - name: outcome
#     label: Outcome
#     type: select
#     choices: [success, failure]
#     default: success
#   - name: seconds
#     label: Seconds
#     type: number
#     default: 3
#     min: 0
#     max: 600
#   - name: exit_code
#     label: Exit code on failure
#     type: number
#     default: 1
#     min: 1
#     max: 255
# --- end scripthub ---
"""Count for a while, then exit 0 or the chosen exit code."""
import argparse
import sys
import time

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
parser.add_argument("--outcome", choices=["success", "failure"], default="success")
parser.add_argument("--seconds", type=int, default=3)
parser.add_argument("--exit-code", type=int, default=1)
args = parser.parse_args()

for n in range(1, args.seconds + 1):
    print(f"step {n} of {args.seconds}", flush=True)
    time.sleep(1)

if args.outcome == "failure":
    print(f"Failing on purpose with exit code {args.exit_code}.", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(args.exit_code)
print("Done.")

#   - name: count
#     label: Count
#     type: number
#     default: 3
#     min: 0
#     max: 100
#   - name: ratio
#     label: Ratio
#     type: decimal
#     default: "0.75"
#     min: 0
#     max: 1
#   - name: verbose
#     label: Verbose
#     type: boolean
#     default: true
#   - name: color
#     label: Color
#     type: select
#     choices: [red, green, blue]
#     default: green
#   - name: features
#     label: Features
#     type: multiselect
#     choices: [logs, metrics, traces]
#     default: [logs, metrics]
#     help: "Repeated flag: --features logs --features metrics"
#   - name: since
#     label: Since
#     type: date
#     default: 2026-01-01
#   - name: run_at
#     label: Run at
#     type: datetime
#     default: 2026-01-01T09:30
#   - name: input_file
#     label: Input file
#     type: file
#     placeholder: C:\path\to\file.txt
#   - name: output_dir
#     label: Output folder
#     type: directory
#     placeholder: C:\path\to\folder
#   - name: mode
#     label: Mode
#     type: select
#     choices: [dev, test, prod]
#     default: dev
#     pass_as: env
#     env_name: TOUR_MODE
#   - name: api_token
#     label: API token
#     type: password
#     pass_as: env
#     env_name: TOUR_TOKEN
#     help: "Never saved; masked in logs and history"
#   - name: region
#     label: Region (fixed)
#     type: text
#     default: eu-west
#     editable_at_runtime: false
#     help: "Locked: always the default"
# --- end scripthub ---
"""Print everything this script received, so you can see how each parameter type arrives."""
import argparse
import os
import sys

print("argv:", sys.argv[1:])
print()

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("target")
parser.add_argument("--title")
parser.add_argument("--notes")
parser.add_argument("--count", type=int)
parser.add_argument("--ratio", type=float)
parser.add_argument("--verbose", action="store_true")
parser.add_argument("--color")
parser.add_argument("--features", action="append", default=[])
parser.add_argument("--since")
parser.add_argument("--run-at")
parser.add_argument("--input-file")
parser.add_argument("--output-dir")
parser.add_argument("--region")
args = parser.parse_args()

for key, value in vars(args).items():
    print(f"{key:<12} {value!r}")
print()
print(f"{'TOUR_MODE':<12} {os.environ.get('TOUR_MODE')!r}  (environment variable)")
token = os.environ.get("TOUR_TOKEN", "")
print(f"{'TOUR_TOKEN':<12} {'*' * len(token) if token else '(not set)'}  (environment variable, password)")

# --- scripthub ---
# name: Find large files
# description: List the largest files under a folder.
# category: Files
# parameters:
#   - name: folder
#     label: Folder
#     type: directory
#     default: .
#     required: true
#   - name: min_mb
#     label: At least (MB)
#     type: number
#     default: 10
#     min: 0
#     max: 1000000
#   - name: top
#     label: Show
#     type: number
#     default: 20
#     min: 1
#     max: 1000
#   - name: pattern
#     label: File pattern
#     type: text
#     default: "*"
#     help: "e.g. *.log"
# --- end scripthub ---
"""Walk a folder and print the largest files, biggest first. Folders it cannot read are skipped."""
import argparse
import fnmatch
import heapq
import os
import sys

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
parser.add_argument("--folder", default=".")
parser.add_argument("--min-mb", type=int, default=10)
parser.add_argument("--top", type=int, default=20)
parser.add_argument("--pattern", default="*")
args = parser.parse_args()

if not os.path.isdir(args.folder):
    sys.exit(f"Not a folder: {args.folder}")

limit = args.min_mb * 1024 * 1024
found, scanned = [], 0
for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(args.folder, onerror=lambda e: print(f"skipped: {e}", file=sys.stderr)):
    dirnames[:] = [d for d in dirnames if not os.path.islink(os.path.join(dirpath, d))]
    for name in filenames:
        if not fnmatch.fnmatch(name.lower(), args.pattern.lower()):
            continue
        path = os.path.join(dirpath, name)
        try:
            size = os.path.getsize(path)
        except OSError:
            continue
        scanned += 1
        if size >= limit:
            found.append((size, path))

print(f"{scanned} files checked under {os.path.abspath(args.folder)}")
if not found:
    print(f"None of them is {args.min_mb} MB or larger.")
for size, path in heapq.nlargest(args.top, found):
    print(f"{size / 1024 / 1024:10.1f} MB  {path}")
